title: Preference-Data Noise: How Label Errors Propagate Into Misaligned Policies

original_idea.body:
# Preference-Data Noise

**Problem:** How controlled label noise degrades alignment under DPO on a small model is underexplored.

**Direction:** Inject flipped-label fractions into HH-RLHF, run DPO, measure refusal/helpfulness/sycophancy. Map degradation-vs-noise curve.

**Why it matters:** Quantifies robustness to label noise in non-lab data. Public data, one GPU.

**Relevant context:** Open Problems in RLHF; HH-RLHF.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain but link to catastrophic risk is somewhat indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: DPO via TRL on public data with controlled noise; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped degradation-vs-noise curve with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public data/models; relevant to crowd/scraped preferences.

low_compute.reasoning: Several small DPO runs on one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Label-noise robustness of DPO is fairly well studied.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: DPO label-noise robustness has substantial prior work.
